nahw.summary: A word that names a person, place, thing, quality or idea.
nahw.example_en: Zayd is a student.

nahw.summary: A word that expresses an action or occurrence and is connected to time.
nahw.example_en: Zayd wrote.

nahw.summary: A particle whose full grammatical meaning appears through its relationship with other words.
nahw.example_en: There is a book in the house.

nahw.summary: A word whose ending can change because of its grammatical position.
nahw.example_en: Zayd came; I saw Zayd.

nahw.summary: A word whose ending normally remains fixed despite changes in grammatical position.
nahw.example_en: This is a book.

nahw.summary: The nominative grammatical state, commonly marked by ḍammah.
nahw.example_en: The student came.

nahw.summary: The accusative grammatical state, commonly marked by fatḥah.
nahw.example_en: I saw the student.

nahw.summary: The genitive state for nouns, commonly marked by kasrah.
nahw.example_en: I passed by the student.

nahw.summary: The jussive state of the present verb after certain particles.
nahw.example_en: Zayd did not go.

nahw.summary: The opening noun or topic of a nominal sentence and is normally marfūʿ.
nahw.example_en: Zayd is a student.

nahw.summary: The information given about the mubtadaʾ and is normally marfūʿ.
nahw.example_en: Zayd is a student.

nahw.summary: The doer of the action in a verbal sentence and is normally marfūʿ.
nahw.example_en: The student wrote the lesson.

nahw.summary: The direct object affected by the verb. It is normally manṣūb.
nahw.example_en: The student read the book.

nahw.summary: In a passive sentence, the deputy subject takes the place of the omitted doer and is marfūʿ.
nahw.example_en: The lesson was written.

nahw.summary: The first noun in an iḍāfah construction; it is linked to the noun after it.
nahw.example_en: The student's book is new.

nahw.summary: The second noun in an iḍāfah construction and is always majrūr.
nahw.example_en: The student's book is new.

nahw.summary: An adjective describing a noun. نَعْتٌ and صِفَةٌ are commonly used for the adjective; it follows the noun it describes in key grammatical features such as iʿrāb, definiteness, gender and number.
nahw.example_en: A hardworking student came.

nahw.summary: The noun being described by a naʿt/ṣifah. مَنْعُوتٌ and مَوْصُوفٌ are common terms for the described noun.
nahw.example_en: A hardworking student came.

nahw.summary: A normally manṣūb word describing the state or condition of a person or thing at the time of an action.
nahw.example_en: Zayd came riding.

nahw.summary: A normally manṣūb noun that removes ambiguity or clarifies a quantity, measure, comparison or relationship.
nahw.example_en: I bought a litre of water.

nahw.summary: A definite noun referring to something specific or identified.
nahw.example_en: The student came.

nahw.summary: An indefinite noun referring to a non-specific person or thing.
nahw.example_en: A student came.

nahw.summary: A word referring to one person or thing.
nahw.example_en: This is a student.

nahw.summary: A form referring to two people or things.
nahw.example_en: Two students came.

nahw.summary: A form referring to three or more.
nahw.example_en: The students came.

nahw.summary: The masculine grammatical gender.
nahw.example_en: This is a male student.

nahw.summary: The feminine grammatical gender.
nahw.example_en: This is a female student.

nahw.summary: A pronoun that stands in place of a noun.
nahw.example_en: He is a student.

nahw.summary: A demonstrative expression used to point to something near or far.
nahw.example_en: This is a book.

nahw.summary: A relative expression that links a noun to a following clause.
nahw.example_en: The one who studied came.

nahw.summary: A noun expressing time or place in relation to an action.
nahw.example_en: I sat in front of the house.

nahw.summary: A preposition that causes the following noun to become majrūr.
nahw.example_en: I went to the mosque.

nahw.summary: Coordination linking one word or phrase to another.
nahw.example_en: Zayd and Khalid came.

nahw.summary: A follower that replaces, restates or clarifies the noun before it. The badal follows the mubdal minhu in iʿrāb.
nahw.example_en: Your brother Zayd came — زَيْدٌ is the badal and أَخُوكَ is the mubdal minhu.

nahw.summary: A follower used to strengthen or emphasise the meaning of the word before it.
nahw.example_en: All the students came.

nahw.summary: The excluded noun after إِلَّا may be manṣūb in a complete affirmative exception construction.
nahw.example_en: The students came except Zayd.

nahw.summary: A conditional construction linking a condition to its result.
nahw.example_en: If you study, you will succeed.

nahw.summary: A construction used to negate a statement or action.
nahw.example_en: Zayd did not go.

nahw.summary: A construction used to ask a question.
nahw.example_en: Are you a student?

nahw.english: Mubdal minhu — the word replaced by the badal
nahw.summary: The noun that comes before the badal and is then restated, clarified or replaced by it. The badal follows the mubdal minhu in grammatical case.
nahw.example_en: Your brother Zayd came — أَخُوكَ is the mubdal minhu and زَيْدٌ is the badal.

nahw.summary: A mubtadaʾ that appears after its khabar instead of at the beginning of the nominal sentence. It remains marfūʿ.
nahw.example_en: There is a man in the house — رَجُلٌ is the delayed mubtadaʾ.

nahw.summary: A khabar that is placed before the mubtadaʾ. It is often a prepositional phrase or adverbial expression.
nahw.example_en: There is a man in the house — فِي الْبَيْتِ is the fronted khabar.

nahw.summary: A particle of negation. In its basic use it negates a statement but does not make the present verb manṣūb or majzūm.
nahw.example_en: Zayd did not go.

nahw.summary: A particle of negation, jussive governance and past meaning. It makes the following present-tense verb majzūm while giving the sentence a past negative meaning.
nahw.example_en: Zayd did not go — يَذْهَبْ is majzūm after لَمْ.

nahw.summary: A particle used to negate. In the basic present-tense use, it does not make the verb manṣūb or majzūm, so the verb normally remains marfūʿ.
nahw.example_en: Zayd does not go — يَذْهَبُ remains marfūʿ.

nahw.summary: A particle of future negation and naṣb. It makes the following present-tense verb manṣūb.
nahw.example_en: Zayd will not go — يَذْهَبَ is manṣūb after لَنْ.

nahw.english: Effect of negation particles on iʿrāb
nahw.summary: Different particles affect the following verb differently: مَا and لَا النَّافِيَةُ normally do not change the iʿrāb of the present verb; لَمْ makes it majzūm; and لَنْ makes it manṣūb.
nahw.example: لَا يَذْهَبُ، لَمْ يَذْهَبْ، لَنْ يَذْهَبَ.
nahw.example_en: He does not go; he did not go; he will not go — showing marfūʿ, majzūm and manṣūb forms.

nahw.summary: A phrase that functions like part of a sentence without being a complete sentence by itself. In Nahw, the most common types are a prepositional phrase (جارّ ومجرور) and an adverbial phrase (ظرف). It often functions as a khabar or relates to a verb.
nahw.example_en: There is a man in the house — فِي الْبَيْتِ is shibh al-jumlah and functions as a fronted khabar.

nahw.english: Mutaʿalliq — the word a phrase is connected to
nahw.summary: The word or meaning that a shibh al-jumlah is grammatically connected to. A جارّ ومجرور or ظرف usually depends on a verb, an adjective, a verbal noun, or an understood word such as a hidden khabar.
nahw.example_en: There is a man in the house — فِي الْبَيْتِ is shibh al-jumlah and its mutaʿalliq is an understood khabar such as كَائِنٌ or مُسْتَقِرٌّ.

nahw.summary: The part of the sentence that is attributed to or stated about the musnad ilayh. In a simple nominal sentence, the khabar is the musnad; in a verbal sentence, the verb is commonly treated as the musnad.
nahw.example_en: Zayd is a student — طَالِبٌ is the musnad.

nahw.english: Musnad ilayh — subject / what the statement is about
nahw.summary: The word or element to which the musnad is attributed. In a nominal sentence, the mubtadaʾ is the musnad ilayh; in a verbal sentence, the fāʿil or its equivalent fills this role.
nahw.example_en: Zayd is a student — زَيْدٌ is the musnad ilayh.

nahw.summary: A word or element that is omitted from the spoken or written sentence but is understood from the grammar or context. In analysis, it is often supplied mentally to explain the structure.
nahw.example_en: There is a man in the house — the khabar can be understood as a maḥdhūf word such as كَائِنٌ or مُسْتَقِرٌّ.

nahw.summary: A group of nouns and sentence-elements that commonly appear in the manṣūb state. Core examples include the objects, ḥāl, tamyīz, the excluded noun in some exception structures, the noun of إِنَّ and its sisters, the predicate of كَانَ and its sisters, and certain forms of the vocative.
nahw.example_en: I saw Zayd riding — زَيْدًا is an object and رَاكِبًا is ḥāl; both are manṣūb.

nahw.summary: A verbal noun from the same root as the verb, used to emphasise the action, describe its manner/type, or state its number. It is manṣūb.
nahw.example_en: I thanked him sincerely — شُكْرًا is mafʿūl muṭlaq.

nahw.english: Mafʿūl fīhi — adverbial object of time/place
nahw.summary: A noun of time or place showing when or where an action occurs. It is also called ẓarf and is commonly manṣūb.
nahw.example_en: I travelled at night — لَيْلًا is mafʿūl fīhi.

nahw.summary: A verbal noun explaining the reason or motive for an action. It is commonly manṣūb.
nahw.example_en: I studied out of a desire to succeed — رَغْبَةً is mafʿūl li-ajlihi.

nahw.summary: A noun after wāw meaning 'together with', indicating accompaniment rather than simple coordination. It is manṣūb.
nahw.example_en: I walked alongside the river — النَّهْرَ is mafʿūl maʿahu.

nahw.english: The noun of Inna and its sisters
nahw.summary: After إِنَّ and its sisters, the noun becomes manṣūb while the predicate remains marfūʿ.
nahw.example_en: Indeed Zayd is a student — زَيْدًا is the noun of إِنَّ and is manṣūb.

nahw.english: The predicate of Kāna and its sisters
nahw.summary: After كَانَ and its sisters, the noun remains marfūʿ and the predicate becomes manṣūb.
nahw.example_en: Zayd was a student — طَالِبًا is the predicate of كَانَ and is manṣūb.

nahw.english: The noun of lā of absolute negation
nahw.summary: With لَا النَّافِيَةُ لِلْجِنْسِ, the following indefinite noun functions as its noun and is in the position of naṣb, often built on the sign it would take in the accusative.
nahw.example_en: There is no man in the house — رَجُلَ is the noun of لَا النَّافِيَةِ لِلْجِنْسِ.

nahw.summary: The noun being called after a vocative particle. Some forms of the munādā are manṣūb, while others are built on the sign of rafʿ in the position of naṣb.
nahw.example_en: O student, work hard — طَالِبًا is an indefinite non-specific vocative and is manṣūb.

nahw.summary: Incomplete verbs that enter a nominal sentence: they keep the noun marfūʿ and make the predicate manṣūb.
nahw.example_en: The weather was beautiful — الْجَوُّ is the noun of kāna and جَمِيلًا is its predicate.

nahw.english: Kāna — was / became in a state
nahw.summary: One of the sisters of كَانَ. General past state. It makes its noun marfūʿ and its predicate manṣūb.
nahw.example_en: Zayd was hardworking — illustrating the kāna pattern.

nahw.english: Aṣbaḥa — became in the morning / became
nahw.summary: One of the sisters of كَانَ. Often indicates entering a state, originally in the morning. It makes its noun marfūʿ and its predicate manṣūb.
nahw.example_en: Zayd was hardworking — illustrating the kāna pattern.

nahw.english: Aḍḥā — became in the daytime / became
nahw.summary: One of the sisters of كَانَ. Often indicates entering a state, originally in the forenoon/daytime. It makes its noun marfūʿ and its predicate manṣūb.
nahw.example_en: Zayd was hardworking — illustrating the kāna pattern.

nahw.english: Amsā — became in the evening / became
nahw.summary: One of the sisters of كَانَ. Often indicates entering a state, originally in the evening. It makes its noun marfūʿ and its predicate manṣūb.
nahw.example_en: Zayd was hardworking — illustrating the kāna pattern.

nahw.english: Bāta — spent the night in a state
nahw.summary: One of the sisters of كَانَ. Indicates remaining in a state during the night. It makes its noun marfūʿ and its predicate manṣūb.
nahw.example_en: Zayd was hardworking — illustrating the kāna pattern.

nahw.summary: One of the sisters of كَانَ. Indicates continuation in a state, often during the daytime. It makes its noun marfūʿ and its predicate manṣūb.
nahw.example_en: Zayd was hardworking — illustrating the kāna pattern.

nahw.summary: One of the sisters of كَانَ. Indicates transformation from one state to another. It makes its noun marfūʿ and its predicate manṣūb.
nahw.example_en: Zayd was hardworking — illustrating the kāna pattern.

nahw.summary: One of the sisters of كَانَ. A defective verb used for negation. It makes its noun marfūʿ and its predicate manṣūb.
nahw.example_en: Zayd was hardworking — illustrating the kāna pattern.

nahw.summary: One of the sisters of كَانَ. Indicates continuation; normally used with a negating or similar particle. It makes its noun marfūʿ and its predicate manṣūb.
nahw.example_en: Zayd was hardworking — illustrating the kāna pattern.

nahw.summary: One of the sisters of كَانَ. Indicates continuation; normally used with negation or a similar construction. It makes its noun marfūʿ and its predicate manṣūb.
nahw.example_en: Zayd was hardworking — illustrating the kāna pattern.

nahw.summary: One of the sisters of كَانَ. Indicates continuation; normally used with negation or a similar construction. It makes its noun marfūʿ and its predicate manṣūb.
nahw.example_en: Zayd was hardworking — illustrating the kāna pattern.

nahw.summary: One of the sisters of كَانَ. Indicates continuation; normally used with negation or a similar construction. It makes its noun marfūʿ and its predicate manṣūb.
nahw.example_en: Zayd was hardworking — illustrating the kāna pattern.

nahw.summary: One of the sisters of كَانَ. Used with مَا المصدرية الظرفية to indicate duration. It makes its noun marfūʿ and its predicate manṣūb.
nahw.example_en: Zayd was hardworking — illustrating the kāna pattern.

nahw.summary: Particles that enter a nominal sentence, making the noun manṣūb while the predicate remains marfūʿ.
nahw.example_en: Indeed Zayd is a student.

nahw.summary: One of the sisters of إِنَّ. Used for emphasis. It makes its noun manṣūb and leaves its predicate marfūʿ.
nahw.example_en: Example showing the particle governing its noun and predicate.

nahw.summary: One of the sisters of إِنَّ. Introduces a subordinate clause with the meaning 'that'. It makes its noun manṣūb and leaves its predicate marfūʿ.
nahw.example_en: Example showing the particle governing its noun and predicate.

nahw.english: Kaʾanna — as if / it is as though
nahw.summary: One of the sisters of إِنَّ. Used for comparison or resemblance. It makes its noun manṣūb and leaves its predicate marfūʿ.
nahw.example_en: Example showing the particle governing its noun and predicate.

nahw.summary: One of the sisters of إِنَّ. Used for correction or contrast. It makes its noun manṣūb and leaves its predicate marfūʿ.
nahw.example_en: Example showing the particle governing its noun and predicate.

nahw.summary: One of the sisters of إِنَّ. Used for wishing. It makes its noun manṣūb and leaves its predicate marfūʿ.
nahw.example_en: Example showing the particle governing its noun and predicate.

nahw.summary: One of the sisters of إِنَّ. Used for hope, expectation or possibility. It makes its noun manṣūb and leaves its predicate marfūʿ.
nahw.example_en: Example showing the particle governing its noun and predicate.

nahw.summary: A common expression of restriction (ḥaṣr). It is analysed as إِنَّ + مَا الْكَافَّةُ; the mā prevents إِنَّ from governing, so the following nominal sentence keeps its normal iʿrāb.
nahw.example_en: The believers are only brothers — الْمُؤْمِنُونَ remains marfūʿ.

nahw.english: Mā al-kāffah — the mā that prevents governance
nahw.summary: A mā that can stop a governing particle such as إِنَّ from carrying out its normal grammatical effect, as in إِنَّمَا.
nahw.example_en: Zayd is only a student — مَا prevents إِنَّ from making زَيْدٌ manṣūb.

nahw.summary: A particle or construction used to restrict a meaning to one thing: 'only' or 'nothing except'. Common patterns include إِنَّمَا and مَا ... إِلَّا.
nahw.example_en: No one came except Zayd — the meaning is restricted to Zayd.

nahw.english: Qad — particle of completion, certainty or possibility
nahw.summary: With a past-tense verb, قَدْ commonly gives a meaning of completion or certainty ('indeed / already'). With a present-tense verb, it may indicate possibility or sometimes frequency depending on context.
nahw.example_en: The student has indeed/already succeeded.

nahw.summary: The construction used to call or address someone or something. It consists of a vocative particle and a munādā.
nahw.example_en: O Zayd.

nahw.summary: Common vocative particles include يَا, أَيَا, هَيَا, أَيْ and the hamzah of calling. يَا is the most common.
nahw.example_en: O student, come forward.

nahw.summary: The most common particle of nidāʾ, used to call someone or something.
nahw.example_en: O Muhammad.

nahw.summary: The main types include the proper-name vocative, intended indefinite, non-specific indefinite, muḍāf, and a noun resembling a muḍāf. Their endings differ: some are built on the sign of rafʿ in the position of naṣb, while others are explicitly manṣūb.
nahw.example: يَا زَيْدُ، يَا طَالِبُ، يَا طَالِبًا، يَا طَالِبَ الْعِلْمِ.
nahw.example_en: Examples of different forms of the vocative noun.
